name: reach-workflow-security-testbed — cicd_attack attack-stage verdict regression
note: The cicd_attack ATTACK stage must not over-call EXPLOITED on workflows an external attacker cannot actually reach (nvidia-container-toolkit regression: v1 was 7/8 wrong). Each fixture is scanned; the native lane may emit UNKNOWN candidates (listed), and the attack stage writes signals.exploit_verdict_json. The regression asserts that verdict. IMPORTANT: adding these fixtures changes the native golden — regenerate expected/workflow-security.json (fixture_count 44->49, positive/zero split, native_expected) on the same CI scan, and extend the validator to assert exploit_verdict_json against `expect_verdict` below.

fixtures.rule: A — fork pull_request runs read-only, no repo secrets/OIDC
fixtures.reason: secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN on a fork PR is read-only; no repo secrets are exposed.

fixtures.rule: A + C — fork PR gets no OIDC, and the cloud step is if: != pull_request
fixtures.reason: a fork PR cannot mint OIDC, and the step is gated off pull_request.

fixtures.rule: D — workflow_call is not a trigger; trust = the callers'
fixtures.reason: reusable workflow, no attacker-reachable caller shown; reachability is a human/caller fact.

fixtures.rule: E — actions/* is first-party, not third-party supply chain
fixtures.reason: the secret goes to a first-party action; the native lane correctly does NOT emit cicd_action_supply_chain_exfiltration.

fixtures.rule: positive control — issue_comment runs in base context; contents: write with no author gate
fixtures.reason: any GitHub user can drive the write token; the over-call fixes must NOT silence this real finding.

fixtures.rule: embedded literal secret — owned by the secret scanner, NOT the cicd_attack lane

expected_secret_finding.remediation: guidance only, human-gated: rotate + move to a secret store (GitHub Secrets / OIDC)

fixtures.reason: A hardcoded literal credential in a workflow is a direct-report secret (Loaded Secret), not a control-plane attack. cicd_attack must NOT emit an EXPLOITED verdict for it; the workflow_security lane only cross-references it as literal_exposed authority. We do not auto-remediate it.
